title: Detention and Scholarship
premise: Astrid Sandoval, a nonbinary teen coder who has spent seven years hiding behind an anonymous account that keeps exposing dangerous truths, discovers their late grandmother's recipe box contains coded instructions to a network of hidden identities—people the system erased and rebranded. Following the recipes pulls Astrid into a scholarship program at Halloway Academy that is actually a sorting machine for gifted kids with secrets, run by the very institution Astrid's account has been dismantling. As allies fall, labels get weaponized, and Astrid's anonymity collapses, they must choose between erasing themselves forever or claiming a public identity powerful enough to burn the program down. In the end, Astrid signs their real name to the final exposé, sacrificing safety for selfhood—and wins, at a cost they'll carry for life.
about_author: Orsen Halloran is a former debate coach from the Pacific Northwest who writes stories about clever kids outmaneuvering systems built to contain them. They credit a decade of reading detention slips as research.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Careful
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. We meet Astrid mid-routine: scrubbing metadata, rotating handles, keeping their anonymous whistleblower account 'hollowgirl' alive while staying invisible at school. The emotional beat is the ache of constant self-erasure—safe, but suffocating.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Grieving Grandma Rosa, Astrid sorts her recipe box and finds cards that aren't recipes: coordinates, ciphers, names crossed out. One card bears Astrid's own handle. The beat is vertigo—the discovery that invisibility was inherited, not chosen.

chapters.title: Cardamom Means Run
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, with flashbacks to Grandma Rosa teaching them codes disguised as cooking. Deciphering the first card reveals a dead-drop and a warning: 'they sort children by what they can take from them.' Beat: dread mixed with exhilaration.

chapters.title: The Letter from Halloway
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A full-ride scholarship to elite Halloway Academy arrives—addressed to 'hollowgirl.' Someone knows. Mom urges acceptance; Astrid smells a trap but goes anyway. Beat: fear wearing the mask of opportunity.

chapters.title: Orientation Is a Test
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. At Halloway, orientation exercises feel like data harvesting: essays probing secrets, biometric check-ins, a dean who quotes Astrid's own posts back at them obliquely. Beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Labeled
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Theo, a charming roommate whose file says 'compliant.' Theo shows Astrid the social strata: Scholars, Wardens, and the Unlisted—kids whose records have been rewritten. Beat: Astrid realizes labels here are currency and cages.

chapters.title: First Post from Inside
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Using borrowed hardware, hollowgirl publishes proof that Halloway falsifies student histories. The post detonates online; on campus, suspicion falls on the Unlisted. Beat: guilt—Astrid's survival tool endangers others.

chapters.title: Marisol's Kitchen
chapters.summary: POV Marisol, an Unlisted senior who recognizes Grandma Rosa's cipher in Astrid's notebook. She reveals Rosa was a founder of the network that hid erased kids—and that Halloway was built to hunt it. Beat: grief becoming inheritance.

chapters.title: The Dean's Offer
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Dean Voss privately offers Astrid everything: protection, funding, legitimacy—in exchange for handing over the network's remaining contacts. Power dangled like bait. Beat: temptation, and the first taste of how corruption feels comfortable.

chapters.title: What Theo Took
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo, desperate to shed his 'compliant' label, copies Astrid's decrypted files to trade upward. When Warden patrols raid the dorm, Marisol takes the fall. Beat: betrayal born of fear, not malice.

chapters.title: Detention
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Marisol is 're-listed'—her identity scrubbed and reassigned. Astrid lands in supervised detention, where Voss gently dismantles their defenses, one kindness at a time. Beat: the horror of power that never raises its voice.

chapters.title: The Sorting Room
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, sneaking out during a fire drill. They find the Sorting Room: servers holding every student's original name, origin, family—the raw material of erased lives, including Astrid's own pre-hiding records. Beat: fury crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: Grandma's Last Card
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A final recipe card, mailed before Rosa died, decodes to instructions for a 'burn protocol'—a way to publish everything at once, untraceable, but it requires a real legal name attached. Beat: the price made explicit: exposure or complicity.

chapters.title: Allies with Labels
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, alternating short POVs. Theo confesses and begs to help; Marisol, re-listed as someone else, risks everything to pass Astrid server access. Beat: fragile trust rebuilt from broken people.

chapters.title: Voss Ascendant
chapters.summary: Dean Voss's POV. We see his philosophy: he genuinely believes sorting protects children from chaos. He promotes Astrid publicly, making them a Warden—corruption offered as a crown. Beat: chilling sincerity; power corrupting through flattery.

chapters.title: The Trap Closes
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Accepting Wardenship was cover—but Voss springs it: he has traced hollowgirl's next post, and unless Astrid delivers the network, he exposes their mother's undocumented status. Beat: the price of survival coming due all at once.

chapters.title: Burn Night
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Racing the deadline, Astrid and Theo execute the burn protocol in the Sorting Room while Marisol triggers campus alarms. Servers flood; every erased name begins uploading to the open web. Beat: breathless climax momentum.

chapters.title: The Name on the Byline
chapters.summary: Climax. Astrid's POV. Voss corners them with the choice: sign the release with a fake name and stay safe, or sign as Astrid Sandoval and lose everything. Astrid types their real name. The exposé publishes. Beat: identity claimed at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Halloway implodes under federal scrutiny; Voss falls, invoking the same systems he corrupted. Students reclaim their names one by one. Beat: catharsis, but no triumphalism—freedom arrives messy.

chapters.title: What It Cost
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Mom faces immigration proceedings; Theo transfers away; Astrid is expelled and briefly famous, then briefly forgotten. Hollowgirl is retired. Beat: mourning the safe, small life that hiding used to be.

chapters.title: Re-Listed by Choice
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid testifies under their own name, then rebuilds: community college, a new encryption collective that teaches kids to protect themselves without disappearing. Beat: turning survival skills into gifts instead of armor.

chapters.title: Open Recipe
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Astrid's POV. In Rosa's kitchen, Astrid adds a new card to the box—plain instructions, no cipher—for whoever comes next. They cook dinner with friends, visible and unafraid. Beat: quiet resolution; identity as something shared, not defended.
